tagline: Grown for the people who ask where it came from.
sector: Retail horticulture: an heirloom specialty nursery and garden centre selling perennials, herbs, shrubs and a short specimen list from its own benches across four planting departments.
founded_place_size: A small heirloom grower in Litchfield County, Connecticut, selling from its own benches, with a growing office and four department benches each tended by a different person.
about: Ferncroft Nursery grows heirloom and specialty stock for gardeners who read the botanical name first. Everything is sold off the bench with a tag that reads like a plant person wrote it. Spring opening is the last Saturday of April, and every plant on the rack needs its tag by then.
audience: Gardeners aged thirty five to sixty five who buy for provenance, read the Latin name, and ask where the stock was grown. They distrust a rack where one tag looks like a different shop.
price_positioning: An heirloom specialty grower at eighteen to ninety five dollars a plant, above the six dollar big-box rack and below a fine-press botanical print. The tag is provenance-led and botanical-forward: the Latin carries, the price sits small, the photograph is a supporting note.

palette.name: Slate Grey
palette.usage: Type: the common name, the pot size and the price, as on ferncroft_hangtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf and ferncroft_benchtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf; it may also carry the nursery mark. Never a ground, band or panel.

palette.name: Fern Green
palette.usage: The botanical Latin and the care icon row, as on ferncroft_hangtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf and ferncroft_benchtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf; it may also carry the nursery mark. Never a ground, band or panel, and never any other line of tag copy.

palette.name: Bench Cream
palette.usage: The tag ground and the only ground colour, as on ferncroft_hangtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf and ferncroft_benchtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf. Never a type colour and never the nursery mark.

palette.name: Terracotta
palette.usage: Hairline rules, one small ornament or the nursery mark only; neither 2025 printer PDF uses it. Never tag copy, a panel or a ground.

palette.name: Bark Brown
palette.usage: The care line, as on ferncroft_hangtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf and ferncroft_benchtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf; it may also carry the nursery mark. Never a ground, band or panel, and never any other line of tag copy.

palette.name: Sage
palette.usage: A panel or mount framing the photograph or its picture area, a hairline rule, or the nursery mark. Never tag copy, never the tag ground, never laid over the photograph.

typography: Ferncroft Nursery runs two faces across four steps. Step 01 is the common name in Trirong Light 300 at 28 pt on 31 pt, tracking -0.01 em, on the 148 by 210 mm hangtag, or 14 pt on the 55 by 85 mm department tag. Step 02 is the botanical Latin in Trirong Light Italic 300 at 15 pt on 17 pt, tracking 0, sitting on the next baseline under the common name with no space between them at exactly 54 percent of its size, or 9 pt on the department tag; italic is used for nothing else. Step 03 is the care copy in National 2 Regular at 9 pt on 13 pt, tracking 0, held to a maximum of 65 characters a line and set at 16 px on screen. Step 04 is the pot size and price in National 2 Regular at 8 pt on 11 pt tracked 0.02 em, sitting small so the Latin carries the tag.
voice: Warm, knowledgeable, unhurried, the voice of a grower. Example line the brand would write: 'Slow to establish, then generous for decades. Give it morning sun and patience.'
brand_assets_status: There are no design files. The two tags the printer ran last spring survive only as press PDFs, and the nursery mark exists only routed and painted into the slate sign at the gate, captured in one handheld photograph. The mark and the printed care icons have to be recovered before they can go anywhere new.
values: Provenance and honesty on the bench: the name on the tag is the right name, and the whole rack reads as one careful hand. Restraint signals quality here.

type_system.tagline: Grown for the people who ask where it came from.

scale.note: The common name on the 148 by 210 mm hangtag, cut like an old botanical plate. Department tags at 55 by 85 mm run this line at 14 pt. Existing sizes kept exactly as the brand already sets them.

The botanical Latin, and the signature move. It sits on the next baseline under the common name with no space between them, at exactly 54 percent of its size: 15 pt under 28 pt on the hangtag, 9 pt under 14 pt on the department tag. Italic is used for nothing else.

scale.sample: Full sun. Leave the seedheads for the finches.
scale.note: Care copy. Maximum 65 characters a line. On screen this line sets at 16 px. Existing size and leading kept.
Pot size, provenance and price. The price sits small and never competes with the Latin. Existing 8 pt kept; leading supplied.

type_system.signature_move: The botanical Latin sits on the next baseline directly under the common name, in Trirong Light Italic 300 at exactly 54 percent of the common name's size with no space between them, and italic is used for nothing else on the tag.
rules: Italic is never used for anything but the botanical Latin.
The Latin always sits on the next baseline under the common name, at exactly 54 percent of its size, with no space between them.
Hangtags at 148 by 210 mm run 28 pt and 15 pt; department tags at 55 by 85 mm run 14 pt and 9 pt.
Care, pot size and price are the only items in National 2 Regular: 9 pt on 13 pt for care, 8 pt for pot size and price, 16 px on screen.
The Latin carries the tag: the price sits small and the photograph is a supporting note.
The whole rack reads as one careful hand: no department sets its own type, and no tag looks like it came from a different shop.
Restraint signals quality here: above the six dollar big-box rack, below a fine-press botanical print.

palette_rules.distribution: Bench Cream is the tag ground and the only ground colour. Tag copy takes three colours, as on ferncroft_hangtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf and ferncroft_benchtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf: the common name, pot size and price in Slate Grey, the botanical Latin in Fern Green, the care line in Bark Brown. The care icons are Fern Green. The nursery mark (fern frond and FERNCROFT NURSERY lettering) is one solid palette colour other than Bench Cream; the type-colour limits govern tag copy, not the mark. Sage may frame the photograph or its picture area as a panel or mount, run as a hairline rule, or carry the mark. Terracotta is for hairline rules, one small ornament or the mark, no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area. Neither accent is ever tag copy or the ground.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the six palette hexes for type, panels, rules, icons or the nursery mark. No tag copy in Sage, Terracotta or Bench Cream, and no nursery mark in Bench Cream. No ground in Slate Grey, Fern Green, Bark Brown, Sage or Terracotta, and no band, block or panel in Slate Grey, Fern Green, Bark Brown or Terracotta.
palette_rules.photography: Photographs keep their own corrected colour and are never tinted, washed or duotoned toward the palette. Foliage keeps the green of its own frame: the plants on dark wet bench timber in ferncroft_variety_03.jpg, ferncroft_variety_08.jpg, ferncroft_variety_10.jpg and ferncroft_variety_15.jpg are not warmed until their leaves turn yellow.
